newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the news conference by Commission President Santer and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi had been postponed from 1715/1615 GMT to 1815/1715 GMT in the Breydel's VIP corner.
Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on the Court of Justice rulings. He said texts were available in his office.
Vale de Almeida said the Commission had decided to launch the first stage of protective measures relating to rice in the overseas territories.

Vale de Almeida briefed on Friday's General Affairs Council. He said discussions would focus on preparation of the Dublin European Council, the inter-governmental conference, the European Economic Area, situation in the Middle East and transatlantic relations. He said that President Santer would also present a medium- and long-term action plan on the Great Lakes area.

Asked about reports that Australia was refusing to sign a trade agreement with the EU in part because it objects to including a clause on human rights, spokesman Peter Guilford said the EU had to remain consistent and Australia should be no exception.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/1121: Commissioner Hans van den Broek protests against closure of Radio B-92.
- IP/96/1132: Accounting: analysis confirms compatibility of EU and international standards.
- Speech/96/321: Speech by Commissioner Hans van den Broek at Peace Implementation Conference.
- Speech/96/321/summary: Summary of speech by Commissioner Hans van den Broek at Peace Implementation Conference.
- Memo/96/115: The European Union - a major client of the WTO.
- Memo/96/116: The Euro-Mediterranean partnership: implementation of the multilateral aspects of the Barcelona declaration.
- EU priorities for World Trade ahead of the first WTO ministerial meeting in Singapore: Reinforcing the open trading system.
